correctness.rationale: The potential-outcome table satisfies the weak null exactly because the six effects sum to zero. The test is reconstructed from the source treatment-control statistic. Exact Fraction arithmetic enumerates all \(20\) actual assignments and all \(20\) sharp-null rerandomizations for each, giving p-value counts \(7\) at \(1/10\), \(3\) at \(1/5\), \(3\) at \(9/10\), and \(7\) at \(1\). Thus \(7\) of \(20\) assignments reject at \(\alpha=0.1\). All \(400\) studentizing denominators are positive, with exact minimum \(246719/2250000\). The bundled checker asserts each of these facts.

value.rationale: The example quantifies a substantive finite-sample gap in a standard asymptotically valid recommendation. A rejection probability \(0.35\) at nominal level \(0.1\) in a balanced six-unit experiment is large enough to matter conceptually, while the exact rational enumeration makes the example reusable as a benchmark for finite-sample weak-null methods. The value is the boundary phenomenon itself, not merely the existence of code or a recomputed table.
